lines.text: Persephone didn't eat six pomegranate seeds. Not in the oldest version.
Hades, god of the underworld, carried Persephone off to be his queen.
Her mother Demeter, goddess of the harvest, was so heartbroken that the crops stopped growing.
Zeus ordered her return. But Hades secretly gave her a pomegranate seed, and anyone who eats food from the underworld must come back.
In the oldest telling, the Homeric Hymn, it's one seed, and she spends a third of the year below. Ovid says seven seeds. The six came much later.
So every year, while Persephone is gone, Demeter grieves. And that's winter.
